description: Discover the schema of a Warehouse or SQL analytics endpoint over INFORMATION_SCHEMA. 'list-tables' returns tables and views (optionally scoped to one --schema); 'describe-table --table [schema.]table' returns one row per column with type, length/precision/scale, nullability, and default. The same two subcommands exist under 'fabio sql-endpoint'. These make schema discovery first-class instead of hand-writing INFORMATION_SCHEMA queries (which is all the remote Fabric DW MCP server's single execute_query tool can do).
notes: Both commands run over the same native-TDS path as 'warehouse query' (SQL-audience token; see the SQL-scope gotcha) and accept a Warehouse OR Lakehouse/SQL-endpoint id. list-tables includes system schemas (queryinsights, sys, INFORMATION_SCHEMA) alongside user schemas — filter with --schema dbo for user tables. describe-table returns the LIST envelope shown above (one row per column); count 0 means the table/schema does not exist. --table accepts 'schema.table', '[schema].[table]', or a bare 'table' (a bare name matches across schemas). All identifiers are injected as escaped N'...' literals, so a schema/table containing a quote cannot be used for SQL injection. Live-verified against a Fabric warehouse and a lakehouse SQL analytics endpoint.
query_examples: fabio warehouse describe-table --workspace <WS> --id <ID> --table dbo.Orders --query "data[].{col: COLUMN_NAME, type: DATA_TYPE, nullable: IS_NULLABLE}"
